newsitem.title: FRANCE: Generale Eaux sees property losses.
newsitem.headline: Generale Eaux sees property losses.

text.p: French utilities giant Cie Generale des Eaux expects property losses this year of 4.6 billion francs, chairman Jean-Marie Messier said on Monday.
The 1996 group profit of 1.8 billion francs annnounced earlier "is after an extra property loss of around 4.6 billion francs," Messier told a news conference.

That property hit was made up of a loss of 1.6 billion francs at the pretax, pre-exceptional level and three billion francs of exceptional charges, he said. The exceptional charges should clear up any future doubts on its property exposure, he said.

"At the end of 1996, Generale des Eaux will not face any questions, even in pessimistic scenarios for the next three years, on any exceptional charges which may arise from its property activities," he said. The group's George V property development arm aims to be profitable from 1997, he said.
The group's average level of property provisioning was around 55-56 percent, of which assets in the South of France were provisioned at 65-70 percent and 85 percent at Cannes.
The property crisis since 1994 has cost the group a total 15 billion francs, he said.
